Gains from competitors are part of market volume rather than sales potential.
tactical_explanations:
When additional buyers remain available, sales potential can sit above today's sales volume. Untapped capture is exactly why potential and volume can diverge for one firm.

So the statement is True.

Customer analysis includes prospective buyers who might purchase if needs are met, not only past purchasers. Excluding prospects would ignore a key source of market potential. The statement's restriction is too narrow.

So the statement is False.

When-customer timing data often reveal seasonal swings in demand across months or weeks. Production planning uses those swings to build stock early, book overtime, or scale capacity before the peak arrives. Claiming seasonal fluctuations cannot inform planning contradicts a standard operational use of purchase-timing analysis. Timing research exists partly to feed operations calendars, not only to describe past sales after the fact.

So the statement is False.

Motive research can reshape offers and messaging so more buyers choose the firm, which can raise market share. Share is not fixed by regulation in the chapter's market setting. Motives therefore can affect share strategies.

So the statement is False.

Gains from competitors belong to sales potential for the firm that might win them. Market volume already counts those sales under the rivals who currently hold them.

So the statement is False.

title: Children Influencing Parent Purchases
context: Review gains from competitors as a component of sales potential for one firm. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Market potential exceeds market volume when category demand from non-buyers remains untapped.
Absolute share is expressed as a percentage of total market sales attributable to one business.
Share in market-potential growth is part of market volume rather than sales potential.
Relative share is expressed as a ratio rather than as a direct percentage of total market sales.
Research institutes may administer questionnaires as primary data collection on behalf of clients.
tactical_explanations:
Non-buyers who could still enter the category leave demand beyond current sales. Market potential therefore can exceed market volume when that untapped demand remains. The statement names the gap correctly.

So the statement is True.

Absolute share is one business's sales as a percentage of total market sales. That percentage reading is the ordinary absolute-share expression.

So the statement is True.

A share of growth in market potential is treated as part of sales potential, not as part of current market volume. Volume records sales already made; potential growth share is forward-looking opportunity for one firm. Parking that growth share inside volume mixes realised totals with prospective gains. The statement misassigns the component.

So the statement is False.

Relative share is a ratio of shares, not another direct percentage of total market sales. Expressing it as a ratio distinguishes it from absolute percentage share.

So the statement is True.

Institutes can run questionnaire fieldwork for clients. That commissioned collection remains primary data gathering even though an external body administers it.

So the statement is True.

title: User Distinct From Buyer
context: Analyze a share in the increase of market potential as part of sales potential. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Trade-body reports may give secondary overview of market size before a firm calculates its own share.
Investors ignore absolute market share because only relative share appears in annual reports.
Relative share compares a firm with the smallest competitor rather than the largest.
Children influencing grocery choices while adults pay illustrates influencer roles in customer analysis.
Users of industrial components may differ from managers who sign supplier contracts in business markets.
tactical_explanations:
Trade-body reports often sketch market size from existing industry data. Firms reuse those secondary overviews before computing their own share from internal sales against the total.

So the statement is True.

Investors do examine absolute market share when judging how large a firm is inside its industry. Relative share adds competitive context, but it does not erase absolute share from investor reading. Claiming investors ignore absolute share is too strong.

So the statement is False.

Relative share compares the firm with its largest competitor, not the smallest rival in the field. The leader comparison is the whole point of the measure: how the firm stands against the strongest player. Using the smallest rival would invent a different ratio and usually inflate the firm's standing. Annual reports and textbooks keep the largest competitor in the denominator for that reason. The statement's smallest-competitor rule therefore fails.

So the statement is False.

Children can steer grocery choices while adults pay at checkout. That split illustrates influencer roles in customer analysis without requiring children to be the legal buyers.

So the statement is True.

In industrial markets, users of components may differ from managers who sign contracts. User and buyer roles can separate in B2B purchasing.

So the statement is True.

title: Retail Versus Online Channel Data
context: Consider a garden-centre group noting that children influence plant-pot choices even though parents complete the checkout payment. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: A questionnaire sent by post is secondary whereas an online questionnaire is primary.
Reading a competitor's published market review creates primary data for the reader's firm.
Preferred use information from what-customer research reduces mismatch between product features and needs.
Market research excludes competition because rivals refuse to share any information.
Children influencing purchases means children must be the legal buyers in B2C markets.
tactical_explanations:
Postal and online questionnaires both gather new answers when run for a research brief. Delivery mode does not make post secondary and online primary. Both can be primary collection methods.

So the statement is False.

Reading a competitor's published review reuses an existing source. That is secondary information for the reader's firm, not primary data creation. Publication by a rival does not convert reading into primary fieldwork.

So the statement is False.

What-customer research on preferred use shows how buyers actually deploy a product. Matching features to those uses reduces the gap between design and need. Product teams can cut unused extras and strengthen valued functions. Preferred-use insight therefore lowers mismatch risk, which is the practical payoff the statement describes.

So the statement is True.

Market research routinely covers competition and industry conditions alongside customers. Rivals may withhold private data, yet published signals, share figures, and observable moves still inform competitive analysis. Excluding competition entirely is false.

So the statement is False.

Children can influence without being legal buyers. Parents or other adults often complete payment in B2C settings. Influence does not force legal buyer status.

So the statement is False.

title: Production Planning From Timing
context: Analyze automotive, industrial, and medical segments as parts of wider component markets. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Weak showroom traffic identified in where-research may trigger stronger dealer support programmes.
Predictable summer demand identified in when-research may trigger earlier inventory builds.
Preference for local suppliers identified in why-research may shape regional marketing messages.
A supplier in the printed circuit boards segment may improve positioning by commissioning a tailored questionnaire before launching an updated product line.
Published trade statistics on the printed circuit boards market can serve as secondary information when estimating total industry sales.
tactical_explanations:
Weak showroom traffic from where-research can push managers toward stronger dealer support. Channel findings are meant to trigger remedies, not only to record empty floors.

So the statement is True.

When-research that flags predictable summer demand lets firms build inventory earlier. Advance stock preparation is a direct operational use of timing patterns.

So the statement is True.

Why-research that finds a preference for local suppliers can reshape regional messages, partner lists, and service promises. Motive insight moves from abstract preference into concrete marketing choices. Regional campaigns that stress local availability follow naturally from that finding. The statement links why-insight to regional messaging correctly.

So the statement is True.

A printed-circuit-board supplier can commission a tailored questionnaire before an updated line launches. That new collection is primary research aimed at positioning. Custom questions beat generic guesses about buyer needs.

So the statement is True.

Published trade statistics on printed circuit boards are existing sources. Reusing them to estimate total industry sales is secondary market information.

So the statement is True.

title: Preference Motives and Market Share
context: Review long-term growth opportunities linked to new applications in technology markets. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: User and buyer must coincide in B2B markets because businesses sign one contract per person.
Channel weakness cannot be detected because customers never reveal where they shop.
Customer analysis in the printed circuit boards market may ask where buyers purchase, when demand peaks, and why they prefer one supplier.
Printed-circuit-board producer sales of 40 million euros inside a 200 million euro market leave an absolute share of 20 per cent.
Price differentiation over the year is unrelated to when-customer purchase patterns.
tactical_explanations:
In B2B markets, users, influencers, and formal buyers can be different people. One contract per person is not required, and user need not equal buyer. Forcing coincidence invents a false rule.

So the statement is False.

Customers do reveal purchase places through surveys, sales data, and channel analytics. Where-research exists precisely to detect weak channels. Claiming weakness can never be detected denies that evidence path.

So the statement is False.

Customer analysis in printed circuit boards can ask where buyers source boards, when demand peaks for projects, and why one supplier is preferred. Those where-when-why strands fit the same research toolkit used in other markets. Segment-specific wording does not change the underlying customer-analysis logic. The statement correctly applies that toolkit to the PCB setting.

So the statement is True.

Forty million over two hundred million equals 0.2, or 20 per cent absolute share. Firm sales divided by market sales produce that percentage. The arithmetic is correct.

So the statement is True.

When-customer patterns across the year are a natural basis for price differentiation by season or peak weeks. Claiming no link ignores that timing use.

So the statement is False.

title: Electronics Market Segment Measures
context: Analyze administering and interpreting large questionnaire programmes as a primary-research cost. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: With 20 per cent absolute share and a leading rival at 40 per cent in printed circuit boards, relative market share equals 0.5.
Market potential in printed circuit boards may exceed current market volume when buyers not yet served could enter the category.
Sales potential for one printed circuit boards firm can exceed its current sales volume through gains from competitors and market growth.
Market volume plus potential customers equals sales volume of one firm.
A supplier in the industrial adhesives segment may improve positioning by running telephone interviews with buyers before launching an updated product line.
tactical_explanations:
Twenty per cent divided by forty per cent equals 0.5. In printed circuit boards, that relative market share follows from absolute share against the leading rival. The ratio matches the definition.

So the statement is True.

Buyers not yet served can still enter the printed-circuit-board category. Their possible demand lifts market potential above current market volume. Untapped entrants are the reason potential can exceed volume here.

So the statement is True.

One PCB firm's sales potential can rise above its present sales volume by winning customers from rivals and by claiming part of market growth. Those components sit inside sales potential in the chapter's breakdown. Current volume alone understates what the firm could sell if competitive gains and expansion materialise. The statement therefore describes a realistic potential above volume.

So the statement is True.

Market volume plus potential customers does not equal one firm's sales volume. Sales volume is the firm's own current sales; market volume is the industry total; potential customers belong to market potential. Adding volume to prospects does not produce a single firm's sales figure.

So the statement is False.

Telephone interviews with adhesives buyers before a launch collect new answers for positioning. That primary fieldwork can improve how the updated line is aimed at real buyer needs.

So the statement is True.

title: Growth Opportunities in New Applications
context: Consider an automotive-parts supplier using secondary data from industry associations before designing a tailored buyer survey. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Published trade statistics on the industrial adhesives market can serve as secondary information when estimating total industry sales.
Customer analysis in the industrial adhesives market may ask where buyers purchase, when demand peaks, and why they prefer one supplier.
Industrial adhesives sales of 57 million euros against a 342 million euro market imply an absolute share of 16.7 per cent.
With 16.7 per cent absolute share and a leading rival at 41.75 per cent in industrial adhesives, relative market share equals 0.4.
Market potential in industrial adhesives may exceed current market volume when buyers not yet served could enter the category.
tactical_explanations:
Published trade statistics on industrial adhesives already exist as industry records. Reusing them to size total sales is secondary information, not new fieldwork.

So the statement is True.

Customer analysis for adhesives can ask where plants buy, when orders peak for construction seasons, and why one binder brand wins contracts. Those where-when-why questions sit inside the same buyer toolkit used in other markets. Segment wording does not change the method.

So the statement is True.

Absolute market share divides firm sales by total market sales. Fifty-seven million euros over a 342 million euro adhesives market is 57/342, which equals about 0.167, or 16.7 per cent. The statement reports that ratio correctly for the industrial adhesives figures given. No rival comparison is required for this absolute calculation.

So the statement is True.

Relative share divides the firm's absolute percentage by the leader's. Sixteen point seven over 41.75 equals 0.4 in adhesives. That head-to-head ratio is exactly what the statement computes.

So the statement is True.

Buyers still outside the adhesives category can enter later. Their possible demand lifts market potential above today's realised market volume in this industry setting.

So the statement is True.

title: Gains From Competitors in Potential
context: Analyze online surveys as a primary research tool that still requires analysis expenditure. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Sales potential minus sales volume always equals zero in growing markets.
Sales potential for one industrial adhesives firm can exceed its current sales volume through gains from competitors and market growth.
A supplier in the commercial laundry equipment segment may improve positioning by analysing responses from an online survey before launching an updated product line.
Published trade statistics on the commercial laundry equipment market can serve as secondary information when estimating total industry sales.
Customer analysis in the commercial laundry equipment market may ask where buyers purchase, when demand peaks, and why they prefer one supplier.
tactical_explanations:
In growing markets, sales potential routinely sits above current sales volume. Subtracting volume from potential therefore need not yield zero; gains and growth leave a positive gap.

So the statement is False.

One adhesives firm can raise sales potential above today's volume by winning rival accounts and by claiming a share of market expansion. Those two routes are standard potential components in the chapter.

So the statement is True.

An online survey before a commercial laundry equipment update collects fresh answers for the launch brief. Analysing those responses is primary research that can sharpen positioning on features buyers actually want. Survey evidence beats guesswork about channel and timing needs. The statement correctly links that fieldwork to better positioning.

So the statement is True.

Trade statistics already published on commercial laundry equipment are existing sources. Using them to estimate industry sales is secondary research, not new interviewing.

So the statement is True.

Laundry-equipment customer analysis may probe purchase points, seasonal peaks, and supplier preference motives. Those strands belong in buyer research for the segment.

So the statement is True.

title: Share in Market Potential Increase
context: Review industry reports published by other businesses as possible secondary sources. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Fifteen per cent absolute share means the market is fifteen times larger than the firm's sales.
Commercial laundry equipment sales of 74 million euros in a 518 million euro market yield a 14.3 per cent absolute market share.
A relative share of one means the firm has one per cent of total market sales.
Primary research is secondary when conducted for another industry and later read by a different firm.
Secondary research is primary when the business pays a fee to access an industry database.
tactical_explanations:
Fifteen per cent absolute share means the firm accounts for fifteen of every hundred sales euros, not that the market is fifteen times the firm's sales. The multiple reading invents a false meaning.

So the statement is False.

Seventy-four million over 518 million equals about 0.143, or 14.3 per cent. Absolute share is firm sales divided by market sales, so the laundry-equipment arithmetic matches the definition.

So the statement is True.

A relative share of one means the firm's absolute percentage equals the largest rival's percentage. It is a ratio of one, not a claim of one per cent of total market sales. Confusing the head-to-head ratio with an absolute one-per-cent reading misstates the metric. Relative share never equals absolute percentage by definition.

So the statement is False.

Primary research stays primary for whoever first collected it for their brief. A later firm reading those results is doing secondary reuse; the original study does not flip labels when the reader changes.

So the statement is False.

Paying a fee for an industry database still reuses existing data. Fee access does not convert secondary sources into primary fieldwork for the paying firm.

So the statement is False.

title: Monetary Expression of Market Size
context: Analyze matching product development to customer needs revealed through what-customer analysis. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Customer analysis dimensions are limited to who and what only.
Market size expressed in pieces sold cannot be compared with market size expressed in euros.
With 14.3 per cent absolute share and a leading rival at 42.900000000000006 per cent in commercial laundry equipment, relative market share equals 0.33.
Market potential in commercial laundry equipment may exceed current market volume when buyers not yet served could enter the category.
Sales potential for one commercial laundry equipment firm can exceed its current sales volume through gains from competitors and market growth.
tactical_explanations:
Customer analysis covers who, what, where, when, and why. Limiting it to who and what alone drops channel, timing, and motive strands the chapter includes.

So the statement is False.

Quantity and value are different units, yet both can describe market size and can be compared across periods once the unit is held fixed. Saying pieces and euros can never be compared invents an absolute ban the chapter does not teach.

So the statement is False.

Relative market share divides absolute share by the leader's share. Fourteen point three per cent against about 42.9 per cent yields roughly 0.33 in commercial laundry equipment. The statement's ratio follows that definition with the given percentages. Absolute figures alone would not produce the rivalry reading without that division.

So the statement is True.

Untapped buyers who could enter laundry equipment still sit outside current volume. Their possible demand raises market potential above realised sales for the category.

So the statement is True.

One laundry firm's sales potential can exceed present volume via rival wins and market growth. Those components sit inside the potential breakdown used in the chapter.

So the statement is True.

title: Quantity Expression of Market Size
context: Consider a components manufacturer that commissions an online survey and telephone interviews to learn what industrial buyers expect from next-generation circuit boards. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: A supplier in the enterprise accounting software segment may improve positioning by hiring an institute to conduct field interviews before launching an updated product line.
Absolute and relative market share always produce identical numerical results.
Published trade statistics on the enterprise accounting software market can serve as secondary information when estimating total industry sales.
Market research institutes collect secondary data because they are independent organisations.
Customer analysis in the enterprise accounting software market may ask where buyers purchase, when demand peaks, and why they prefer one supplier.
tactical_explanations:
Hiring an institute for field interviews before an accounting-software launch gathers new data for positioning. Commissioned fieldwork is primary research that can improve the updated line's aim.

So the statement is True.

Absolute share is a percentage of the whole market; relative share is a ratio against the leader. Those numbers coincide only by accident, not always. Treating them as identical invents a false rule.

So the statement is False.

Published trade statistics on enterprise accounting software already exist as industry sources. Reusing them to estimate total sales is secondary information rather than fresh interviewing. Secondary work is appropriate precisely when published figures can size the market. The statement places those statistics correctly in that secondary role.

So the statement is True.

Independence of an institute does not decide whether data are primary or secondary. Institutes often collect new primary data for clients; secondary status turns on reuse of existing sources, not on organisational independence.

So the statement is False.

Accounting-software customer analysis can ask purchase channels, demand peaks, and preference motives. Those questions belong in buyer research for the segment.

So the statement is True.

title: Percentage Share of One Business
context: Analyze timing analysis that supports differentiated pricing across seasons or months. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Small firms always prefer primary research because it is cheaper than secondary sources.
For enterprise accounting software, 91 million euros of producer sales in a 728 million euro market imply an absolute share of 12.5 per cent.
With 12.5 per cent absolute share and a leading rival at 25 per cent in enterprise accounting software, relative market share equals 0.5.
Market potential in enterprise accounting software may exceed current market volume when buyers not yet served could enter the category.
Why-customer motives are recorded only after sales fall to zero.
tactical_explanations:
Primary fieldwork is often costlier than reusing secondary sources. Small firms do not always prefer primary because it is cheaper; that cost claim is backwards.

So the statement is False.

Ninety-one million over 728 million equals 0.125, or 12.5 per cent absolute share. Producer sales divided by market sales give that percentage for enterprise accounting software.

So the statement is True.

Relative share puts 12.5 per cent against a leader at 25 per cent, which equals 0.5. The ratio shows the firm at half the leader's absolute weight in accounting software. That head-to-head reading is what relative share is designed to show. Absolute percentages alone would not reveal the rivalry gap without this division, and the arithmetic matches the statement.

So the statement is True.

Software buyers not yet in the category can still adopt later. Their possible demand lifts market potential above current market volume in enterprise accounting software.

So the statement is True.

Why-customer motives are studied while sales are healthy, not only after they hit zero. Waiting for collapse invents a false timing rule for motive research.

So the statement is False.

title: Absolute Share Without Rival Detail
context: Review motive analysis explaining preference for one brand over close substitutes. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Where-customer data show factory locations of suppliers rather than customer purchase points.
Sales potential for one enterprise accounting software firm can exceed its current sales volume through gains from competitors and market growth.
A supplier in the organic breakfast cereals segment may improve positioning by designing a primary study around channel preferences before launching an updated product line.
Published trade statistics on the organic breakfast cereals market can serve as secondary information when estimating total industry sales.
Customer analysis in the organic breakfast cereals market may ask where buyers purchase, when demand peaks, and why they prefer one supplier.
tactical_explanations:
Where-customer data track where buyers purchase, not where suppliers locate factories. Factory maps answer a production question, not the customer-channel question.

So the statement is False.

An accounting-software firm's sales potential can exceed current volume through gains from competitors and through a share of market growth. Those routes are standard potential components.

So the statement is True.

Designing a primary study around channel preferences before an organic breakfast cereal launch collects new answers for positioning. Channel insight can reshape retail placement and promotions for the updated line. Primary design beats recycling unrelated reports. The statement correctly ties that study to improved positioning.

So the statement is True.

Published trade statistics on organic breakfast cereals are existing sources. Using them to estimate industry sales is secondary market information rather than new interviews.

So the statement is True.

Cereal customer analysis may ask where shoppers buy, when demand peaks, and why one brand wins. Those strands fit the buyer-research toolkit for the category.

So the statement is True.

title: Customer Characteristics in Market Research
context: Consider a household detergent producer that promotes one standard formula nationwide without tailoring messages to regional income differences. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Market segmentation divides a market into relatively homogeneous subgroups of customers who share relevant characteristics.
Geographic segmentation groups customers according to where they live or operate, such as a city and its surrounding area.
Demographic segmentation uses measurable social characteristics such as age, gender, education level, and income level.
Psychographic segmentation reflects attitudes, values, lifestyle interests, and willingness to pay for particular product philosophies.
Market segmentation requires every customer in a subgroup to be identical in all personal characteristics.
tactical_explanations:
Market segmentation splits a market into subgroups that are relatively alike on traits that matter for marketing. Shared relevant characteristics define those homogeneous clusters.

So the statement is True.

Geographic segmentation sorts buyers by where they live or operate, such as a city plus its surrounding area. Location, not income or lifestyle, is the grouping key.

So the statement is True.

Demographic segmentation uses measurable social traits: age, gender, education, and income are classic examples. Those variables can be counted and compared across groups without reading attitudes or purchase frequency. Marketers use them because they are observable and often available in census or survey data. The statement lists that demographic toolkit correctly.

So the statement is True.

Psychographic segmentation turns on attitudes, values, lifestyle interests, and willingness to pay for particular product philosophies. Soft preference traits, not postal codes, define the cut.

So the statement is True.

Segments need relative homogeneity on relevant traits, not identity on every personal characteristic. Requiring total sameness invents an impossible standard for useful groups.

So the statement is False.

title: Geographic Segmentation by Location
context: Analyze geographic segmentation based on location such as city and surrounding area. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Geographic segmentation classifies customers by income level and education rather than by location.
Demographic segmentation is defined by lifestyle attitudes and values rather than age or income.
Psychographic segmentation is defined solely by postal district and city boundaries.
Behavioural segmentation ignores how customers buy or use products and focuses only on gender.
Behavioural segmentation distinguishes customers by how they buy or use products, such as occasional versus heavy use.
tactical_explanations:
Geographic segmentation classifies by location, not by income or education. Those social measures belong to demographic cuts, so the statement swaps categories.

So the statement is False.

Demographic segmentation is built on age, gender, education, and income. Lifestyle attitudes and values define psychographics instead. Swapping those definitions mislabels the demographic cut.

So the statement is False.

Psychographic segmentation reflects attitudes, values, and lifestyle interests. Postal districts and city boundaries are geographic variables, not psychographic ones. Defining psychographics solely by map lines collapses two distinct segmentation bases into one false rule. Location belongs under geographic segmentation.

So the statement is False.

Behavioural segmentation focuses on how customers buy or use products. Gender is a demographic trait, so treating behaviour as gender-only ignores purchase and usage patterns.

So the statement is False.

Behavioural segmentation separates occasional from heavy users by purchase and usage intensity. That usage distinction is exactly the behavioural cut described in the statement.

So the statement is True.

title: Demographic Segmentation Variables
context: Review demographic segmentation using age, gender, education level, and income level. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: A useful segment should be measurable so that its size and purchasing power can be estimated.
A useful segment should be profitable so that serving it is worthwhile for the business.
A useful segment should be accessible through communication channels and distribution channels that can reach it.
A segment is measurable only when every member has been individually interviewed.
A segment is profitable whenever it is large, even if serving it costs more than the revenue gained.
tactical_explanations:
A useful segment must be measurable so managers can estimate size and purchasing power. Without those estimates, planning spend and capacity lacks a numerical base.

So the statement is True.

Profitability requires that serving the segment be worthwhile: expected revenue should cover the cost of tailored offers. Large but loss-making groups fail this criterion.

So the statement is True.

Accessibility means communication and distribution can actually reach the subgroup. A measurable, profitable segment still fails if ads and retail paths cannot touch it. Channels that connect to the buyers are therefore part of the usefulness test, alongside size and profit checks. The statement names that reach requirement correctly for a useful segment.

So the statement is True.

Measurability allows estimates from samples, sales data, or statistics. Interviewing every member individually is not required for a segment to count as measurable.

So the statement is False.

Sheer size does not guarantee profit if serving costs exceed revenue. Profitability turns on net return, not headcount alone for the segment.

So the statement is False.

title: Psychographic Segmentation and Values
context: Analyze psychographic segmentation reflecting attitudes, values, and lifestyle interests. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: A useful segment should be durable in the sense that it does not change too quickly to support planning.
A segment is accessible if it is profitable, regardless of whether communication or distribution can reach it.
Targeting is the process of evaluating each segment's attractiveness and selecting one or more segments to enter.
A target market is a group of people or businesses toward whom a firm markets goods, services, or ideas with a strategy designed for their specific needs and preferences.
Positioning is the process by which marketers try to create an image or identity in the minds of their target market.
tactical_explanations:
Durability means the segment stays stable enough to support planning. Rapid churn that outruns strategy cycles fails that usefulness test for marketers.

So the statement is True.

Accessibility is about reach through communication and distribution. Profitability alone cannot make a segment accessible if no channel touches the buyers. Conflating the two criteria is wrong.

So the statement is False.

Targeting evaluates how attractive each segment is and then selects one or more to enter. It sits after segmentation has drawn the subgroups and before positioning shapes the offer. Choosing where to compete is the heart of targeting, not redrawing the map of the market. The statement states that evaluation-and-selection role correctly.

So the statement is True.

A target market is the people or businesses a firm markets to with a strategy built for their needs and preferences. Specific needs, not the whole population, define the focus.

So the statement is True.

Positioning tries to create an image or identity in the minds of the target market. That mental placement is the chapter's positioning definition for marketers.

So the statement is True.

title: Behavioural Segmentation Patterns
context: Consider a sportswear brand offering distinct product lines for occasional joggers and for competitive athletes based on usage intensity. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: A durable segment must never change over time in order to qualify for targeting.
After segments are identified and a target market is chosen, positioning clarifies which product meets the demands of the targeted subgroup.
Targeting means dividing the market into subgroups, while segmentation means choosing which subgroup to enter.
Mass marketing ignores different market segments and offers the same product to all customers.
Positioning occurs before segmentation and targeting in the marketing strategy sequence.
tactical_explanations:
Durable means stable enough for planning, not frozen forever. Segments may shift slowly and still qualify; a never-change rule invents an absolute ban.

So the statement is False.

Once segments exist and a target is chosen, positioning clarifies which product meets that subgroup's demands. Image and identity work follow targeting, not replace it.

So the statement is True.

Segmentation divides the market into subgroups; targeting chooses which of those subgroups to enter. The statement reverses the two labels. Mixing the verbs invents a false sequence and would leave managers dividing when they should be selecting. Correct order keeps division first and choice second, before any positioning work begins.

So the statement is False.

Mass marketing ignores segment differences and pushes the same product to all customers. One offer for everyone is the mass approach described in the chapter.

So the statement is True.

The usual sequence is segmentation, then targeting, then positioning. Putting positioning first contradicts that marketing strategy order for the firm.

So the statement is False.

title: Homogeneous Subgroups in Segmentation
context: Analyze how segmentation divides relatively homogeneous subgroups within a broader market. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Under mass marketing, a product is promoted to all segments in almost the same way.
Mass marketing is often applied to everyday products such as pens, pencils, soaps, personal hygiene products, and detergents.
Mass marketing offers different tailored products to each identified market segment.
Mass marketing allows a business to produce a relatively large number of identical products and sell them to a relatively large market.
Economies of scale arise when a large number of identical products is produced and some costs do not increase in direct proportion to output.
tactical_explanations:
Under mass marketing, promotion treats segments almost alike with one shared approach. Near-uniform messaging across the market is the mass pattern.

So the statement is True.

Everyday staples such as pens, soaps, hygiene goods, and detergents often suit mass marketing because many buyers share similar basic needs. The statement's product list fits that everyday use case.

So the statement is True.

Mass marketing offers the same product to the whole market rather than tailored variants for each segment. Differentiated offers belong to segment marketing. Claiming mass marketing supplies different tailored products to each segment swaps the mass and segment definitions. Uniformity, not customisation per cluster, is the mass rule.

So the statement is False.

Mass marketing supports producing many identical units for a large market. Scale of identical output is part of the mass logic for everyday goods.

So the statement is True.

Economies of scale appear when identical output rises and some costs do not climb in lockstep with volume. Shared costs spread across more units of output.

So the statement is True.

title: Measurable Segment Criterion
context: Review the criterion that market segments should be measurable in size and purchasing power. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Mass marketing promotes the same product differently to every segment with highly customised campaigns.
Economies of scale mean that every cost rises in direct proportion to output as production increases.
Increased total output of an identical product can reduce cost per unit because shared costs are divided across more units.
Economies of scale always raise cost per unit when total identical output increases.
Grouping buyers by adult men and women of all ages alone is geographic segmentation because demographics describe place.
tactical_explanations:
Mass marketing promotes one product in almost the same way everywhere, not with highly customised campaigns per segment. Customisation contradicts the mass approach.

So the statement is False.

Economies of scale mean some costs do not rise in direct proportion to output. Claiming every cost rises proportionally denies the scale effect the chapter describes.

So the statement is False.

When identical output increases, shared factory and overhead costs divide across more units, so cost per unit can fall. That spreading of fixed or joint costs is the mechanism behind lower unit cost at higher volume. Managers watch total output of the same product precisely for this unit-cost effect. The statement captures that output-to-unit-cost link correctly for identical products.

So the statement is True.

Economies of scale lower, rather than raise, cost per unit as identical output grows. Claiming they always raise unit cost reverses the concept taught here.

So the statement is False.

Grouping by adult men and women of all ages is demographic, not geographic. Demographics describe people traits such as age and gender, not place on a map.

So the statement is False.

title: Profitable Segment Criterion
context: Analyze the criterion that market segments should be profitable for the business to serve. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Mass marketing can be inflexible and make it harder to react to particular changes in some target markets.
Segment marketing means offering different products to one or more segments after some segmentation.
Grouping buyers in an Austrian city and its surrounding commuter area is psychographic segmentation because location reflects personal values.
Targeting buyers unwilling to pay the full price of a brand-new device is behavioural segmentation because attitudes are the same as purchase frequency.
Distinguishing occasional users rather than intensive daily operators is demographic segmentation because usage is a social characteristic like age.
tactical_explanations:
Mass marketing's one-size approach can be inflexible when particular target markets shift. Reacting to niche changes is harder under a uniform offer.

So the statement is True.

Segment marketing offers different products to one or more segments after segmentation has identified them. Differentiation by subgroup is the segment approach.

So the statement is True.

An Austrian city and its commuter belt form a geographic cut based on location. Psychographics turn on attitudes and values, not map lines. Calling that city-commuter grouping psychographic mislabels a geographic segment. Place defines the subgroup here, while income or lifestyle would belong under other bases entirely.

So the statement is False.

Unwillingness to pay full price for a new device is an attitude or value stance, hence psychographic. Behavioural cuts track purchase and usage frequency, not payment willingness alone.

So the statement is False.

Occasional versus intensive daily use is behavioural segmentation. Usage intensity is not a demographic social characteristic like age or education.

So the statement is False.

title: Accessible Segment Criterion
context: Consider a craft brewery selling specialised seasonal ales only to enthusiasts willing to pay premium prices in a narrow taste category. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Segment marketing focuses limited resources on segments where the firm has strategic fit with customer needs and wants.
Niche marketing focuses on particular segments and often on subgroups within broader segments through more segmentation.
Many small businesses employ niche marketing because they cannot produce the quantity required for a mass market.
A business specialising in a certain field may target only selected segments of a market rather than the whole market.
A niche specialist that serves a segment well can become a market leader regardless of firm size.
tactical_explanations:
Segment marketing concentrates limited resources where strategic fit with customer needs is strongest. Focused fit beats scattering effort across every cluster.

So the statement is True.

Niche marketing goes further into particular segments and often into subgroups inside broader segments. Extra segmentation depth is part of the niche path.

So the statement is True.

Many small firms lack the capacity for mass-market volumes, so niche marketing lets them serve narrower groups they can supply. Quantity limits push them toward focused segments rather than undifferentiated national coverage. Specialisation matches resource constraints. The statement links small-business scale to niche practice correctly.

So the statement is True.

A specialist may target only selected segments instead of the whole market. Selective focus is normal when expertise fits particular clusters of buyers.

So the statement is True.

A niche specialist that serves its segment well can lead that niche regardless of overall firm size. Leadership follows fit, not headcount across the industry.

So the statement is True.

title: Durable Segment Criterion
context: Analyze the criterion that market segments should be durable rather than changing too quickly. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Targeting is the first step toward an effective marketing strategy before the marketing mix is applied to serve the target market.
The marketing mix is applied as a second step to serve the needs of the chosen target market.
Grouping buyers in an Austrian city and its surrounding commuter area illustrates geographic segmentation because location defines the subgroup.
A segment of an Austrian city and its surrounding commuter area is automatically profitable whenever it can be named on a map.
Describing customers as adult men and women of all ages illustrates demographic segmentation using measurable population characteristics.
tactical_explanations:
Targeting comes first in building strategy before the marketing mix is applied to serve the chosen market. Selection precedes mix design for the firm.

So the statement is True.

After the target is chosen, the marketing mix is the second step that serves those needs. Product, price, place, and promotion follow targeting.

So the statement is True.

Buyers in an Austrian city and its surrounding commuter area are grouped by location. That place-based cut is geographic segmentation. Commuter belts and city cores share a spatial definition rather than an attitude or income definition. City-plus-commuter examples are textbook geography cuts. The statement therefore illustrates geographic segmentation correctly.

So the statement is True.

Naming a city-commuter area on a map does not prove the segment is profitable. Profitability still requires revenue above serving costs for that geography.

So the statement is False.

Adult men and women of all ages are demographic descriptors. Age and gender are measurable population characteristics for that demographic cut.

So the statement is True.

title: Targeting Selected Segments
context: Review targeting as the selection of segment or segments a business chooses to enter. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: A segment of adult men and women of all ages is accessible whenever it is measurable, even if no channel reaches them.
A segment of buyers unwilling to pay the full price of a brand-new device is durable only if preferences never shift, making short-term trends irrelevant.
Targeting buyers unwilling to pay the full price of a brand-new device reflects psychographic segmentation based on attitudes and preferences rather than location alone.
Distinguishing occasional users rather than intensive daily operators is behavioural segmentation because purchase and usage patterns differ within the product category.
Mass marketing to an Austrian city and its surrounding commuter area requires a different product formula for every neighbourhood street.
tactical_explanations:
Measurability does not guarantee accessibility. Without channels that reach adult men and women of all ages, the segment remains unreachable despite good size estimates.

So the statement is False.

Durability allows slow change; it does not demand that preferences never shift. Short-term noise can be ignored without requiring permanent freeze of the price-sensitive device segment.

So the statement is False.

Buyers unwilling to pay full price for a brand-new device are grouped by attitude toward price and novelty. That preference stance is psychographic, not a pure location cut. Targeting them therefore reflects psychographic segmentation based on willingness-to-pay attitudes. The statement places the cut in the right category.

So the statement is True.

Occasional versus intensive daily operators differ in purchase and usage intensity. That pattern difference is behavioural segmentation within the product category.

So the statement is True.

Mass marketing to a city-commuter area uses one offer, not a different formula for every street. Street-level customisation contradicts mass logic for that geography.

So the statement is False.

title: Evaluating Segment Attractiveness
context: Analyze how targeting evaluates each segment's attractiveness before commitment. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Niche marketing to buyers unwilling to pay the full price of a brand-new device means selling one identical product to the entire national market.

Niche marketing concentrates on a narrow subgroup, not on selling one identical product to the entire national market. National uniformity is mass marketing, not niche.

So the statement is False.

Segment marketing differentiates offers across subgroups. Ignoring differences and pushing one undifferentiated item is mass marketing, so the statement mislabels segment work.

So the statement is False.

Positioning still matters after geographic segmentation because the firm must place an image for the chosen behavioural subgroup. Completing a location cut does not finish strategy. Occasional versus intensive users still need a clear product identity in their minds. Calling positioning unnecessary after geography invents a false stopping rule for the sequence.

So the statement is False.

Survey and sales data can estimate size and purchasing power for an Austrian city-commuter segment. Those estimates satisfy measurability without interviewing every resident.

So the statement is True.

Adult men and women of all ages are profitable only when expected revenue exceeds serving costs. Size alone does not settle the profit test for that group.

So the statement is True.

title: Positioning and Market Identity
context: Consider a cleaning-products company unable to react quickly when one regional segment shifts toward eco-certified alternatives under a single mass-market formula. Evaluate the following economic assertions:

So the statement is False.

When those channels work, the segment meets the reach criterion even if it is narrower than the mass market. Communication and distribution access are the test. The statement states that accessibility condition correctly.

So the statement is True.

Strategic fit with adult men and women of all ages calls for concentrating resources on that segment, not spreading evenly across every segment in the economy.

So the statement is False.

Tiny customised batches rarely undercut mass unit costs. Claiming they always yield lower unit cost than identical mass runs reverses typical cost logic.

So the statement is False.

title: Segmentation Targeting Positioning Sequence

Durability does not require zero change, only enough steadiness to justify investment. Planning cycles need that relative stability. The statement links usage durability to planning correctly.

So the statement is True.

Valuing environmental reuse of second-hand goods is an attitude, hence psychographic. Behavioural segmentation tracks purchase frequency and usage, not that value stance alone.

So the statement is False.

Seasonal versus year-round purchasing is behavioural. Usage timing is not a demographic trait like age or education level among buyers in the category.

So the statement is False.

Niche marketing to environmental-reuse buyers concentrates on a narrow subgroup whose specialised preferences justify a focused offer. Narrow depth is niche practice here.
